pharm: Recombinant humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds free IgE, reducing free IgE levels and down-regulating high-affinity IgE receptors on mast cells and basophils, blunting allergic and inflammatory responses.
quick: Allergic asthma/nasal polyps: 75-375 mg SC every 2 or 4 weeks, dosed by baseline IgE and body weight; chronic urticaria: 150 or 300 mg SC every 4 weeks
Subcutaneous injection; not related to meals
Limited data; IgG crosses placenta. Use only if clearly needed; registry data reassuring
IgG is present in milk in low amounts and poorly absorbed orally; generally considered compatible
No specific dose adjustment (cleared via reticuloendothelial system, not renal)
Anaphylaxis (observe after injection), do not use for acute bronchospasm, malignancy signs
summary: Omalizumab is a recombinant humanized anti-IgE monoclonal antibody used for moderate-to-severe persistent allergic asthma inadequately controlled by inhaled corticosteroids (in patients with a positive perennial aeroallergen test and elevated IgE), chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, chronic spontaneous urticaria refractory to antihistamines, and IgE-mediated food allergy. For asthma and nasal polyps it is dosed 75-375 mg subcutaneously every 2 or 4 weeks based on pretreatment serum total IgE and body weight; for chronic urticaria it is 150 or 300 mg every 4 weeks regardless of IgE/weight. It carries a BOXED WARNING for anaphylaxis, which can occur after any dose (including the first) and may be delayed; patients should be observed after administration and equipped to recognize and treat anaphylaxis. It is not for acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus.
indications: Moderate to severe persistent allergic asthma (>=6 years) inadequately controlled with inhaled corticosteroids, with positive perennial aeroallergen skin/in vitro reactivity
Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps inadequately controlled with nasal corticosteroids (adults)
Chronic spontaneous (idiopathic) urticaria (>=12 years) refractory to H1-antihistamines
IgE-mediated food allergy (reduction of allergic reactions including anaphylaxis after accidental exposure) in adults and children >=1 year

dosage.d: 75-375 mg subcutaneously, determined by baseline serum total IgE (IU/mL) and body weight using the dosing tables

Dose not dependent on serum IgE or body weight

dosage.d: 75-600 mg subcutaneously per dosing table by total IgE and weight
dosage.n: Adjunct to allergen avoidance; not for emergency treatment of allergic reactions

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection only; doses greater than 150 mg should be divided across more than one injection site
Administer in a healthcare setting prepared to manage anaphylaxis; observe patients for an appropriate period after injection
Reconstitute lyophilized vial with sterile water for injection; the prefilled syringe formulations require no reconstitution
Do not use to treat acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus
Do not abruptly stop corticosteroids upon initiation; taper under medical supervision
moa: Omalizumab is a recombinant DNA-derived humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that selectively binds to free human immunoglobulin E (IgE) at the same site (Cepsilon3 domain) that IgE uses to bind the high-affinity Fc-epsilon-RI receptor. By binding circulating free IgE, it prevents IgE from attaching to mast cells and basophils, lowering free IgE levels and, over time, down-regulating Fc-epsilon-RI receptor expression on these cells. This limits the release of allergic mediators and reduces the magnitude of the IgE-mediated allergic and inflammatory response. It does not bind IgE already bound to receptors and therefore does not cause mast cell or basophil degranulation.

absolute: Severe hypersensitivity reaction to omalizumab or any ingredient in the product
relative: Acute asthma exacerbation, bronchospasm or status asthmaticus (not indicated)
Active parasitic (helminth) infection or high geographic exposure risk
History of anaphylaxis to other triggers (heightened vigilance)
monitor: Anaphylaxis after each injection (may be delayed)
Eosinophilic conditions / vasculitis (eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis)

preg: There are limited human data. Omalizumab is an IgG1 antibody and crosses the placenta, increasingly in the second and third trimesters. Pregnancy registry (EXPECT) data have not shown a clear increase in major malformations. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed; do not initiate solely to manage acute asthma in pregnancy.
lact: Human IgG is present in breast milk; omalizumab is expected to be present in low amounts and to be degraded in the infant's gastrointestinal tract with minimal systemic absorption. Breastfeeding is generally considered compatible; consider the benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother's clinical need.
renal: No formal studies in renal impairment. Omalizumab is cleared via the reticuloendothelial system and IgG degradation rather than the kidney, so no specific dose adjustment is recommended.
hepatic: No formal studies in hepatic impairment; elimination is through hepatic IgG degradation and the reticuloendothelial system. No specific dose adjustment is provided.

major: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions identified for omalizumab itself
moderate: Concomitant systemic or inhaled corticosteroids - do not abruptly discontinue; taper gradually when omalizumab is started
minor: Anthelmintic therapy may be less effective in patients at risk of helminth infection while on omalizumab
interactions.diagnostics: Serum total IgE rises after dosing (bound complexes) and stays elevated up to ~1 year; total IgE measured during therapy cannot guide redosing - use pretreatment IgE for dose determination.

serious: Anaphylaxis and anaphylactoid reactions (may be delayed)
Malignant neoplasms (observed numerical imbalance in trials)
Eosinophilic conditions / eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (often on corticosteroid reduction)
emergency: Anaphylaxis (urticaria, angioedema, throat/tongue swelling, bronchospasm, hypotension, syncope)

monitoring: Observe patients after each injection for anaphylaxis; ensure availability and patient training in epinephrine auto-injector use
Use pretreatment serum total IgE and weight to determine asthma/nasal polyp dosing (not levels during therapy)
Monitor asthma control and lung function; do not abruptly stop corticosteroids
Watch for eosinophilic conditions/vasculitis when reducing oral corticosteroids
Watch for signs of malignancy over long-term use
counsel: Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) can happen after any injection - even the first - and may be delayed by hours; learn the warning signs and how to use an epinephrine auto-injector, and seek emergency care if they occur
This is a preventive treatment - it will not relieve a sudden asthma attack; keep using your rescue inhaler and do not stop your other asthma/steroid medicines unless told to
Injections are given in the clinic; you may be asked to stay for observation afterward
Tell your doctor if you have a history of parasitic infections or are traveling to high-risk areas
Report rash, joint pain, fever, persistent shortness of breath, or any signs of a new mass/lump
pk: Free IgE suppressed within ~1 hour of dosing; clinical asthma benefit over weeks
Subcutaneous absorption slow; peak serum concentration at ~7-8 days
Effect maintained with every 2- or 4-week dosing; total IgE remains elevated up to ~1 year after stopping
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; protect from light; reconstituted vial used promptly
pearls: BOXED WARNING: anaphylaxis can occur after any dose (including the first), may be delayed (up to 24 h or more), and has occurred even in patients with no prior reactions - observe after injection and provide epinephrine and an anaphylaxis action plan
Asthma/nasal polyp dosing depends on PRETREATMENT total IgE and body weight; serum IgE measured during treatment is artificially elevated and must not be used to adjust dosing
Not a rescue therapy - never use for acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus
Reducing oral corticosteroids may unmask eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss) - watch for vasculitic rash, worsening pulmonary symptoms, neuropathy
Effectiveness against helminths may be reduced; monitor at-risk patients
missed: Omalizumab is given on a fixed every-2-week or every-4-week schedule in a clinical setting. If an injection is missed, contact the clinic to reschedule as soon as possible and resume the prescribed interval; doses are not doubled to make up.
overdose: A maximum tolerated dose has not been established; single intravenous doses up to 4,000 mg have been administered without evidence of dose-related toxicity, and chronic dosing up to 44 mg/kg/month was tolerated. In suspected overdose, monitor for adverse effects (including anaphylaxis) and provide supportive, symptomatic care.
